messages.subject: Freedson equation
parts:
Hi all,

 

I'm now conducting a project using Actigraph and we found your R package GGIR can used for analysis.

 

We originally planed to use Freedson equation to calculate the number of minutes spent in MVPA.  It needs the age of the subject for calculation.

 


 

We found that using GGIR package, we can also get the time spent in MVPA but age of subject isn’t needed. May we know which formula does the package use? And could I use Freedson equation in the package? 


Thanks so much!!

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Freedson equation
parts:
In short, MVPA is calculated based on an acceleration (metric ENMO) threshold you specify as user, which by default is 100.
There is a distinction between bouted and non-bouted MVPA.

The calculation in part 2 was described in  https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/25361583 
The calculation in part 5 was described in https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/28367987 
Further, you can search the google group and the GGIR package documentation for the term "bout" or "bout metric" to get more information.

For the Freedson equation you need Actigraph counts. Freedson's MVPA calculation is not part of GGIR because GGIR does not calculate or process Actigraphy count data. GGIR was developed to facilitate the processing of raw data accelerometry in order to help the research field to move away from these notorious count data.

Best, Vincent
